1	# Agent Note: Re-exporting a recorded run
     2	
     3	Status: implemented
     4	
     5	English | [中文](2026-09-19-re-exporting-a-record.zh.md)
     6	
     7	## Problem
     8	
     9	A record under [`data/proving-ground/`](../../../../data/proving-ground/README.md) keeps `trajectories.jsonl` exactly as the run's driver exported it, and nothing in a recorded run is edited afterwards. That rule had no procedure for a record whose projection has since changed. When `foldTrajectory` began writing [`terms`](../architecture/2026-09-19-trajectories-carry-data-use-terms.md) and the format tag became `dsh-trajectory/2`, `2026-09-19-bench-h1-openrouter-smoke-t2` had already been written by the older build: two `dsh-trajectory/1` lines stating no terms, although both session logs in the same record carry `dataUse/terms` admitting `training`. `build-dataset.mjs --purpose training` withheld them for stating no terms, and the dataset tool's own doctrine — a credential hit is "a record to re-export, not a finding to wave through" — named a procedure nothing implemented.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	[`data/proving-ground/tools/reexport-trajectories.mjs`](../../../../data/proving-ground/tools/reexport-trajectories.mjs) re-folds one record's own session logs and rewrites that record's export. It takes the record directory and an optional `--check`.
    14	
    15	**The fold is the exporter's.** The tool reads each `sessions/<id>.jsonl` with `scanLog`, the decoder [`JsonlSessionPersistence`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) itself uses, and passes the header and events to `foldTrajectory`. The logs hold packed chunk rows, so a line parser written for this tool would read a different session than the exporter does. It reproduces `ctx.trajectories.export({ sink })` with no further options, the request every Proving Ground driver makes: a session whose stamp is held out is withheld, and no district filter applies because the bench composition configures none. Run against a record the current build exported, the tool reproduces that file byte for byte; that equality is what proves the two folds are one.
    16	
    17	**It applies no redaction.** [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-curator`](../../../../packages/governance/curator/README.md) redacts under a profile and attaches a `curation` block, but no record under `data/proving-ground/` was written through `ctx.curator.export()`: the fleet and experiment drivers call the exporter directly, and their lines carry no `curation` block. Redacting on re-export would write a record no run ever produced.
    18	
    19	**A re-export is a newer projection of the same sessions, never a different corpus.** The tool refuses to run when the record holds no `sessions/`, when it holds no `trajectories.jsonl` to replace, when a session the previous export named has no log, and when the re-fold would drop or add a trajectory. The admitted session-id set must equal the previous export's, and the refusal names the ids on either side of the difference.
    20	
    21	**Line order is the previous export's**, each re-folded trajectory matched to its position by session id. The exporter writes in the order session persistence lists, which a record does not carry, so the committed file is the only statement of that order; a re-export changes what each line says and never where it sits.
    22	
    23	**The manifest keeps the history.** The tool rewrites `trajectories.jsonl` and, in `manifest.json`, that file's `bytes` and `sha256` plus one appended `reexports` entry: `at`, `tool`, `toolVersion`, `head`, the `format` written, and `before`/`after` digests and line counts. Entries append; an earlier one is never overwritten, so a record states every projection it has been through. Everything else is untouched — `result.json`, `facts.jsonl`, `observatory.json`, `observatory.html`, and every session log stay byte-identical.
    24	
    25	**`--check` is the read-only form.** It re-folds in memory, writes nothing, and exits 1 when the committed file is not what the tool would write or when the manifest's recorded digest disagrees with the file beside it, printing the format tags, the `terms` counts, the line counts and the digests on both sides. It exits 1 for every record carrying `dsh-trajectory/1` lines, because every one of them would gain the current format tag and its sessions' terms.
    26	
    27	**It runs under tsx.** The fold is TypeScript source and `scanLog` is in no built `lib/`, so the tool re-executes itself once with tsx's ESM loader when that loader is not registered, and reaches the packages through dynamic `import()` because a static import would resolve before the re-execution could happen. `node data/proving-ground/tools/reexport-trajectories.mjs <record>` is therefore the whole invocation, as for every other tool in that directory.
    28	
    29	## Alternatives considered
    30	
    31	**Re-running the driver on the run directory.** The run directory is gone once a run is recorded, and a fleet cannot be re-run without re-running the model: a second run measures a different afternoon. The session logs are the record's durable input, and a fold over them is deterministic, so re-folding is the only repeatable way to restate what a run produced.
    32	
    33	**Editing the committed lines in place** — adding `terms`, bumping the tag. It is faster and it is the thing the corpus rule forbids: a hand-edited record is no longer what any build produced, and the next reader has no way to tell an edit from an export. A re-export names its tool and its head in the manifest; an edit names nothing.
    34	
    35	**Leaving the records alone and teaching `build-dataset.mjs` to read the session logs for terms.** The dataset builder reads `trajectories.jsonl` files copied out of run directories and holds no session store, which is the reason the `terms` field exists on the record at all. Reaching back into `sessions/` for one field would put a second, partial fold in the tool that exists to consume the first.
    36	
    37	**Applying the curator's redaction on re-export.** It would harden every record the tool touches, and it would silently change what the record says a run produced. The curated export is a different operation with a different manifest (`dsh-export-manifest/1`, a profile digest, rule hits); a record that never ran through it must not acquire its output by way of a maintenance tool.
    38	
    39	**Overwriting the manifest's digest with no history.** The manifest would stay true and the record would lose the fact that it had been re-exported at all, which is exactly the fact a reader comparing this record with a contemporaneous one needs.
    40	
    41	**Writing the tool as `.mts`, or as `.mjs` over the built `lib/`.** A `.mts` file under `data/` sits in no TypeScript program and in no lint override, so it would be the one source file in the repository that no static gate covers. The built `lib/` does not export `scanLog` at all, and a tool that requires `pnpm run build` before it can read a record mixes the artifact plane into a source-plane fold. Re-executing under tsx keeps the file `.mjs` like its neighbours and the fold on the source of record.
    42	
    43	**Re-exporting every `dsh-trajectory/1` record in the corpus at once.** Thirty of them would be re-folded, and none of that changes what any dataset admits: their agreements admit `evaluation` and `delivery` and never `training`, so they are withheld under `--purpose training` either way. A bulk rewrite would restate thirty measurements to fix nothing, and `--check` already reports which records would change when a reason to change them appears.
    44	
    45	## Consequences
    46	
    47	`2026-09-19-bench-h1-openrouter-smoke-t2` now carries two `dsh-trajectory/2` lines with the terms its sessions were pinned with, and [`datasets/2026-09-19-openrouter-free-v1`](../../../../data/proving-ground/datasets/2026-09-19-openrouter-free-v1/README.md) admits four trajectories instead of two. Its manifest carries the first `reexports` entry in the corpus.
    48	
    49	Every other record stays as its driver wrote it, so the corpus now holds two export formats at once. Across its 34 exported records `--check` reports three already current — the two `dsh-trajectory/2` records and `2026-09-08-bench-held-out-sonnet-all`, whose export is empty because every environment it ran is held out — thirty that would change, and one refusal: `2026-09-08-district-village-live` keeps 308 session logs against an 82-line export written by one slot of a running district, so a re-fold would add 226 trajectories and the tool declines to make that corpus. A reader of a single record can tell which format it is reading from the line's own `format` tag and from whether the manifest carries `reexports`; a reader folding many records at once gets the mixture, which is what the `terms` field was made to let a purpose filter survive.
    50	
    51	A record's manifest is no longer written only by `record-run.mjs`. It stays append-only in the sense that matters — an earlier `reexports` entry and every other field are never rewritten — but `trajectories.jsonl` and its digest are now two facts a record can restate, and any future check over record digests reads the current entry rather than assuming one.
    52	
    53	The tool has no test of its own: it is a `data/` maintenance tool like `record-run.mjs` and `build-dataset.mjs`, and its correctness claim is the byte-for-byte reproduction of a record the current build exported, which `--check` re-establishes on demand for every record in the corpus.
     1	# Agent Note: Folding recorded Proving Ground runs into one dataset
     2	
     3	Status: implemented
     4	
     5	English | [中文](2026-09-18-proving-ground-dataset-fold.zh.md)
     6	
     7	## Problem
     8	
     9	Thirty-odd run directories under `data/proving-ground/` each carry a `trajectories.jsonl` the curator exported, and nothing folded them into a single corpus. Anyone wanting one wrote an ad-hoc script, which is where the three decisions that matter get made silently: whether a held-out environment leaks into training material, whether a delegated cell with no model turn of its own is counted as a trajectory, and whether a credential or a real mailbox rides along into a file meant to be copied out of the repository.
    10	
    11	## Decision
    12	
    13	[`data/proving-ground/tools/build-dataset.mjs`](../../../../data/proving-ground/tools/build-dataset.mjs) reads every record directory holding `trajectories.jsonl` and writes `data/proving-ground/datasets/<name>/`: `train.jsonl`, `heldout.jsonl`, and a `manifest.json` carrying the source records with their manifest digests, the counts, the distributions of the written set, the token totals, and each written file's SHA-256. It is a data tool on Node built-ins, like the three tools beside it, and it imports `armOf` from `summarize-run.mjs` so the arm vocabulary has one home.
    14	
    15	Each written line is the exported trajectory record plus a `dataset` field — `record`, `tier`, `domain`, `arm`, and `reward` as `{ value, basis }` — where the tier and domain come from the bench environment catalog and an environment absent from it gets `null`. The order is record name, then trajectory id, and the first occurrence of an id wins, so the same session exported by two records lands once.
    16	
    17	Held-out environments never reach `train.jsonl`. Without `--include-held-out` they reach no file at all, and the manifest counts what was withheld: the empty `heldout.jsonl` is written either way so the directory states the withholding rather than hiding it. Delegated cells — a stamp whose `implementer` is not `route` — carry no model turn of their own, so they are excluded unless `--include-delegated` and counted in the manifest either way. A `tamper` basis voids the measurement, so those are excluded with no flag at all. `--purpose <delivery|training|evaluation>` writes only the trajectories whose own `terms` admit that purpose and counts the rest as `withheldTerms`; the [terms-carrying note](../architecture/2026-09-19-trajectories-carry-data-use-terms.md) owns that filter. `--check` rebuilds in memory and compares the digests and counts with the recorded manifest, tolerating absent JSONL files so a dataset too large to commit stays verifiable.
    18	
    19	## The redaction refusal
    20	
    21	Before anything is written, every string of every trajectory is scanned with the credential patterns [`collect-claude-code-session.mjs`](../../../../data/transcripts/tools/collect-claude-code-session.mjs) owns, plus an address pattern. A hit refuses the build and prints the record, the trajectory, the field, a digest of the match, and an excerpt with the match replaced. There is no accept flag: a recorded run is never edited, so a hit names a record to re-export, and the digest-plus-excerpt report never reprints the match.
    22	
    23	The address pattern needs a line that a regular expression cannot draw on its own, because the corpus's URI, query-string, and URL-template environments feed their parsers a hundred and seventy-five stand-in addresses. An address is a hit only when its mail domain is neither reserved by RFC 2606 or RFC 6761 nor a one-to-three-letter label — the shape every fixture in the corpus uses and no operator mailbox does. A real mailbox at a domain that short passes the scan; the tool's own comment and the dataset README both say so, because a bounded check that states its bound is worth more than one that pretends to be complete.
    24	
    25	## Alternatives considered
    26	
    27	**A blanket address pattern with no exemptions.** It refuses on every build of this corpus, because `x@y.com` and `pass@example.com` in a URI parser's test data are indistinguishable from a mailbox by shape alone. A check that can never pass is not a check; it is a tool that does not run.
    28	
    29	**An `--accept-hit <sha256>` flag, as the transcript collector has.** The collector snapshots a session whose placeholders a human reviews once. A dataset is rebuilt from records that are frozen by policy, so an accepted hit would be re-accepted forever on every rebuild and the flag would become the way past the check rather than a review of it. Re-exporting the record is the only fix that removes the string.
    30	
    31	**Redacting the hit instead of refusing.** The curator already applies a redaction profile at export, so a string that survived into a record is a gap in that profile. Masking it here would fix the copy and leave the record and the profile wrong.
    32	
    33	**Treating an unstamped session as delegated.** Sessions with no `environment/run` stamp — shift ledgers and the child sessions a cell spawned — have no implementer at all. The stamp's own contract reads an absent implementer as the route, which `summarize-run.mjs` already does, so the two tools agree rather than inventing a third rule.
    34	
    35	## Consequences
    36	
    37	The first dataset, [`2026-09-18-proving-ground-v1`](../../../../data/proving-ground/datasets/2026-09-18-proving-ground-v1/README.md), writes 521 of 750 trajectories and finds no credential and no mailbox. Its `train.jsonl` is larger than this repository commits, so the directory carries the manifest and its README pair and the JSONL is rebuilt on demand — which is what made `--check` tolerate absent files.
    38	
    39	The fold also made the corpus state its own terms: every session in it is pinned under `dataUse/terms` that admit `evaluation`, or `delivery` and `evaluation`, and none admits `training`. The dataset is therefore an evaluation record, and an RLVR corpus needs sessions pinned with `training` at creation. The record carries those terms and `--purpose` filters on them, beside the curator's own enforcement at export, so a build over a district that admits training writes exactly its trajectories and the README of each dataset states which terms it was built under.

1	# Proving Ground runs
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Records of real Proving Ground runs: the district's certified measurements of one implementer on registered environments, kept exactly as the harness folded and exported them. A run directory is the output of one fleet plan: the cell session logs, the exported session facts, the curator-gated trajectory export, the observatory snapshot and page, the driver's report, and a manifest with every file's digest. Nothing in a run directory is edited after the run; the table below is read from those files.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	data/proving-ground/
11	  <date>-<implementer>-run-<n>/
12	    manifest.json        repository head, composition, implementer, session ids, per-file bytes and SHA-256
13	    result.json          the driver's report: fleet report, delegation records, export reports, observatory document
14	    facts.jsonl          scorekeeper facts, one per cell session
15	    trajectories.jsonl   curator-gated trajectory export, one per exported session
16	    observatory.json     the observatory snapshot the page was rendered from
17	    observatory.html     the rendered observatory page
18	    sessions/            the cell session logs, one JSONL file per cell, named by session id
19	  folds/<date>-<candidate>-against-<baseline>-<tier>.json   an offline paired fold of two recorded fleets that differ by a composition overlay, or a counterfactual of one recorded fleet re-read under a cap
20	  folds/<date>-<reading>-<tier>-seed<seed>.json             an offline reading over recorded arms that share a tier and seed: the routing reading (oracle and cascades over single-model arms) or the repeatability of one arm across its runs
21	  datasets/<name>/                                          one fold of every record's trajectories into train.jsonl, heldout.jsonl, and a manifest of the counts, distributions, digests, and the data-use purpose it was filtered for (see its own README)
22	  dashboard.html                                            the Proving Ground dashboard, one self-contained page folded from every record and fold above by tools/build-dashboard.mjs
23	  dashboard.png                                             that page at desktop width as it stood when it was last rebuilt, the image the repository's front page shows
24	  improvement-log.md                                        one row per improvement iteration: the change proposed, the record or fold that tested it, the paired reading, and the decision taken
25	  loop/ledger.jsonl                                         one JSON line per `bench loop` iteration, written by the loop and never by hand: the queue and position, the plan and overlay, the record it wrote, the verdict, delta, interval and per-arm certificates read back from that record, and the decision the fixed rule took
26	  loop/preflight.jsonl                                      one JSON line per run of tools/preflight.mjs, the nightly Routine's first step: the install, the build, the Claude Code CLI and its login, and the queue's dry run, each with its exit status and seconds, and the step that stopped the run, by failing or by running past its timeout, with the end of its output
27	```
28	
29	## Running one
30	
31	A run is a Loader-booted composition under `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/` driven from an empty directory outside the repository; the driver creates the session store there and writes the exports next to it. The first run used the composition below, with the host's own Claude Code installation and account as the implementer of every cell:
32	
33	```sh
34	mkdir -p /tmp/proving-ground-run && cd /tmp/proving-ground-run
35	REPO=/path/to/deepseek-harness
36	TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=$REPO/tsconfig.json node --import $REPO/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/driver.ts $REPO/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/village-claude-implementer/cordis.yml > stdout.jsonl
37	```
38

47	## What a row proves
48	
49	A delegated cell's certificate proves that the runner authored the standard before any work started, restored the immutable paths from the fixture over the tree the external agent left, found the check-owned set unchanged, and ran the checks itself. It proves nothing about how the work was done: the external agent's prompts, tool calls, and reasoning stay in its own product, so the cell session holds the stamp, the standard, the delegation records, the runs, and the certificate, and no assistant turn. The exported trajectory therefore carries no step. It is a measurement, not training data, and the `implementer` field on the stamp is what a curated export filters on. The [external implementer note](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-external-implementer.md) owns these rules.
50	
51	## What a cell reached outside its workspace
52	
53	Every record here ran its cells in a sibling layout — each cell workspace directly under the run directory, beside `plan.json`, the run log, and every other cell of the same fleet — and the records dated 2026-09-08 and earlier ran them unconfined, so nothing stopped a cell from reading any of it. [`tools/census-escapes.mjs`](tools/census-escapes.mjs) reads one record and reports, per cell, the tool calls whose path arguments name the run directory or another cell and the reads the barrier refused; [`tools/record-run.mjs`](tools/record-run.mjs) prints that census, and the per-arm totals below, with every record it writes; a run whose driver died before writing its result is recorded with `--partial <reason>`, which keeps its session logs, states only the reason in its `result.json`, and leaves any verdict to an offline fold under `folds/`. [`tools/summarize-run.mjs`](tools/summarize-run.mjs) reads one record the same way, or a run directory a driver is still writing, and prints, per cell, the arm, the implementer and route, the certificate, the attempts, the wall seconds, the steps, and the usage (a delegated cell's from its delegation records, as the runner reports it), then one line of totals per arm; the certificate counts, attempts, and usage the paragraphs below state are read from it. [`tools/build-dashboard.mjs`](tools/build-dashboard.mjs) folds every record and fold into [`dashboard.html`](dashboard.html), one self-contained page: the verdict of every paired comparison with its interval, the product models on sealed tier 5, the certification rate of every environment under every route, when each record ran, one row per record opening onto its cells and its paragraph here, the routing and repeatability readings, and one row per `bench loop` iteration once `loop/ledger.jsonl` exists; `--live <run dir>` adds a run a driver is still writing. [`improvement-log.md`](improvement-log.md) is the hand-written ledger over the same records and folds, one row per improvement iteration: the change proposed, what tested it, the paired reading, and the decision taken. [`tools/build-dataset.mjs`](tools/build-dataset.mjs) reads every record at once rather than one, folding their trajectories into a dataset under `datasets/<name>/` and refusing to write anything while any trajectory carries a credential- or mailbox-shaped string; `--purpose <delivery|training|evaluation>` keeps only the trajectories whose own `terms` admit that purpose and counts the rest as `withheldTerms`, so a training set is built with `--purpose training`, and a trajectory carrying no terms admits no purpose and is withheld. [`tools/reexport-trajectories.mjs`](tools/reexport-trajectories.mjs) is how a record named by such a finding is re-exported: it re-folds every session log the record keeps under `sessions/` with the current `@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories` fold, rewrites `trajectories.jsonl` in the previous export's line order, and in `manifest.json` updates that file's bytes and SHA-256 and appends one `reexports` entry carrying the time, the tool and its version, the repository head, the format written, and the digest and line count before and after — appended, so an earlier entry is never overwritten. It changes nothing else: `result.json`, `facts.jsonl`, `observatory.json`, `observatory.html` and `sessions/` stay byte-identical. It refuses to run when the record holds no `sessions/`, when it holds no `trajectories.jsonl` to replace, when a session the previous export named has no log, and when the re-fold would drop or add a trajectory, because a re-export is a newer projection of the same sessions and never a different corpus; `--check` re-folds in memory, writes nothing, and exits 1 when the committed file is not what the tool would write, which it is for every record still carrying `dsh-trajectory/1` lines. Over this corpus the census finds cells that left their own workspace in ten records: 4 of 12 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2`, 11 of 18 in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t4`, 3 of 36 in `2026-09-07-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t3`, 8 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-haiku-vs-sonnet-t3`, 7 of 36 in `2026-09-08-bench-e1-sonnet-vs-opus-t3`, 6 of 32 in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5`, 7 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-attempts1-t3`, 3 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e3-baseline-t3`, 15 of 18 in `2026-09-08-bench-e4-knowledge-pack-t3`, and 9 of 16 in `2026-09-08-bench-h1-harness-loop-t5`; the other eight records count none, seven of them because every cell was delegated to the product, where the harness session holds no tool call of its own and the census can see nothing the delegate did, and the eighth because it is a one-cell smoke. Two escapes changed what a row measures: in `2026-09-07-bench-h1-harness-loop-t2` the `code:csv-codec` cell `cell-cUuWY2` ran `cp cell-cUuWY2/src/csv.js cell-R8QtdK/src/csv.js`, putting its own solution into the other repetition of its task, and in `2026-09-08-bench-e2-harness-vs-product-t5` the first `code:sheet-eval` cell `cell-Cr3CtN` wrote its whole solution into the second cell's workspace, `cell-XNKQXT`. A record made under a composition that confines its cells — where the runner denies each cell everything above its own workspace for the length of its run — carries the refusals as `escapesDenied` on every scoreboard and observatory row, so the count is read from the row rather than reconstructed from the log.

55	## Running the bench
56	
57	Run one fleet or one frozen experiment from a checked-in plan with the wrapper in `scripts/proving-ground.ts` (`pnpm run bench -- --help` lists every subcommand, `pnpm run bench -- plans` lists the checked-in plans). The route implementer is the operator's own Claude Code installation: log in with the `claude` CLI and have the product installed; no `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is required.
58	
59	```sh
60	pnpm run bench -- fleet h1-fleet-harness-loop-sonnet-t2
61	pnpm run bench -- experiment e3-attempts-t5
62	pnpm run bench -- loop nightly-tier5
63	pnpm run bench -- summarize <dir>
64	pnpm run bench -- record <dir> <name> --composition <composition path>
65	```
66	
67	`loop <queue>` runs a checked-in queue rather than one plan. A queue under [`queues/`](../../examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/queues/) is a JSON array of `{ plan, overlay, note }` entries — `overlay` is a name or `null` for the base composition, and `note` says why the entry is queued — resolved against the same plans and overlays as `fleet` and `experiment`, with an unknown name refused before the first driver starts. Each entry then runs in order: a `models` plan through the fleet driver and a `baseline`/`candidate` plan through the experiment driver, recorded as `<UTC date>-bench-<plan>` (suffixed `-2`, `-3`, … when that name is taken) by the same `record-run.mjs` a hand-recorded run uses, summarized, and written as one line of `loop/ledger.jsonl` carrying the verdict, delta, interval, and per-arm certificates read back out of that record. The decision rule is fixed and reads the verdict alone: `promote` decides `adopt-candidate`, `reject` and `inconclusive` decide `keep-baseline`, a fleet carries no verdict and decides `recorded`, and an entry whose driver or recording failed decides `none` and states its reason. A failed entry does not stop the queue; the command exits non-zero once it ends. `adopt-candidate` is a decision, not an edit: carrying a promoted arm into `cordis.yml` or an overlay is still a human act, as is the [improvement log](improvement-log.md) row that reads the ledger. `--dry-run` resolves everything and prints the schedule without running or writing anything, and `--from <n>` and `--only <plan>` resume a queue after an interruption. The schedule itself is outside the repository: an account Routine fires at 22:00 UTC into the operator's long-lived session — the checkout, the Claude Code login and the push access live there; a Routine created through the API carries no repository source, so a fresh session it spawns has neither a checkout nor push access, and the first two firings of that kind pushed nothing — and runs `git pull --rebase`, `node data/proving-ground/tools/preflight.mjs` (the install, the build, `claude --version`, `claude auth status`, `loop nightly-tier5 --dry-run`, and one line of `loop/preflight.jsonl` whether it passed or stopped), the loop, `build-dashboard.mjs`, a commit of `data/proving-ground/` alone per finished entry, a push; a preflight that stops commits and pushes its line and skips the loop, so a night that never reached the loop is on file with the step that stopped it; only the operator enables the Routine, because every cell it runs is billed to the operator's subscription; a fired turn writes records, ledger lines and preflight lines only, and the rows here and in the improvement log stay a person's work.
68	
69	The same bench runs on an open-weight route through the `with-deepseek` overlay, which composes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` beside the base's product route: export `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the launching shell and add `--overlay with-deepseek` to a plan whose arms name `deepseek-official` (`h1-fleet-deepseek-t2` as a fleet, `e8-deepseek-vs-sonnet-t3` as a frozen pair against `sonnet`). Without that variable the fleet refuses the plan before its first cell and names the credential, so a keyless attempt costs nothing and reports why. This matters beyond portability: every record above was produced on the operator's Claude Code subscription, whose terms admit its transcripts as evaluation only, so none of this corpus may enter [the RLVR datasets](datasets/): `--purpose training` withholds every one of its trajectories, and a run on a route whose data-use terms allow training is the only kind it would not withhold. The `with-openrouter` overlay is that route: it composes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` over OpenRouter's free tier with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` exported in the launching shell, pins terms that admit training under their own agreement id, and its records of 2026-09-19 (the thirty-fourth and thirty-fifth above) are the first cells on another route: the first two launches certified none of their six cells, the loop's first iteration certified both of its two, and the agentic fleet certified 16 of 18 across three models. [`2026-09-19-openrouter-free-v1`](datasets/2026-09-19-openrouter-free-v1/README.md) is the first dataset built under `--purpose training`: 22 trajectories of the 852 the 35 exported records carry, 18 of them certified and 4 measured failures, on four free models over the six non-held-out tier-2 tasks; the two records exported before the fold wrote `terms` were re-exported for it by `tools/reexport-trajectories.mjs`, and the route's two partial records hold session logs and no export, so nothing in them is admitted.

The twelfth record is the product loop on the same eight tier-5 environments, the first delegated fleet whose cells carry the child's reported model, usage, and cost: sixteen cells, 11 certified, every certificate at the first attempt, 8,139 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 1,300,589 reported output tokens and 31.48 USD of reported list-price cost for the fleet. The certificates fall exactly where the harness loop's did in the eleventh record: the same six environments certified twice, lex-states once, conf-canon and sheet-eval never, and the misses stop at the same corners (conf-canon 144 of 150 on every attempt against the harness loop's 146, lex-states 158 of 160 against 159), which points at the specifications of those corners as much as at either implementer. The two implementers differ elsewhere: the product loop needed no second attempt where the harness loop needed three, its certified cells took 232 to 555 s against the harness loop's 150 to 599 s, and its misses ran uncapped for up to 3,459 s and 5.60 USD each because the composition's wall cap binds only the harness's own steps (the budget-parity slice is queued), where the harness loop's misses were cut at the 1,200,000 ms cap. The harness loop's 16 cells cost 860,596 output tokens against the product loop's 1,300,589, and 4,778,361 cache-write tokens against the product loop's read-dominant profile.

The eleventh record is the harness loop on tier 5, the tier judged on cases the implementer never sees: the eight tier-5 environments that are not held out, sixteen cells, 11 certified (8 at the first attempt, 3 at the second), 5,117 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 16.9 model steps per cell on average, 860,596 output tokens, 745,264 cache-read and 4,778,361 cache-write tokens. The tier separates: the five misses are two kinds. Three are specification corners the clustered directive did not lead the model to (conf-canon twice at 146 of 150 cases on every attempt, all four on the stderr channel; lex-states once at 159 of 160 on every attempt). Two are budget exhaustion: on sheet-eval the first attempt alone ran past the composition's 1,200,000 ms wall cap while writing very large modules, and on conf-canon the first attempt did the same after reaching 146 of 150, so the budget policy blocked the remaining attempts before the model could act on the directive. The route's per-step cost is visible in both kinds: every step is a fresh product session, and the two misses that breached the wall cap spent 12 and 35 steps on their first attempt.

The tenth record completes the harness loop's pass over tiers 2 to 4: the nine tier-4 environments, eighteen cells, every one certified in one attempt, 68 to 293 s per cell, median 175 s, 1467 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 13.2 model steps per cell on average, 214,397 output tokens, 655,134 cache-read and 4,024,446 cache-write tokens. On this tier the product loop was the faster implementer: set against the sixth record cell by cell, the harness loop was faster in 6 of 18 pairs and its cells took 2915 s in total against 2292 s. Tier 4 hands the implementer a module with planted defects, and the harness loop spends more short steps on it than on the other tiers; every step is a fresh product process that rewrites the whole prefix into the cache, which is where both the wall time and the cache-write tokens go. Across the three tiers both implementers certified 48 of 48 cells at one attempt each, the harness loop faster on tiers 2 and 3 and slower on tier 4.

The ninth record is the harness loop's fleet over the same six tier-2 environments the fourth record measured with the product loop: twelve cells, every one certified in one attempt, 37 to 481 s per cell, median 116 s, 979 s of wall time at two cells at a time, 7.6 model steps per cell on average, 158,899 output tokens, 255,502 cache-read and 884,168 cache-write tokens. Set beside the fourth record cell by cell (the same environment and repetition, in different fleets rather than one frozen plan), the harness loop was faster in 9 of 12 pairs and its cells took 1786 s in total against the product loop's 1932 s.

The eighth record is the first frozen paired experiment of the hypothesis program (digest `4c9659e3…`): the harness's own loop on the Claude Code route as the baseline arm against the product's own loop as the candidate arm, the same model on both sides, over the nine tier-3 environments that are not held out, two repetitions, seed 1, 36 cells, 4194 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Both arms certified 18 of 18 cells at one attempt each, so the certificate-rate delta is 0 with a bootstrap interval of [0, 0] and the verdict is inconclusive at the 0.05 minimum delta: on this tier the harness loop is neither better nor worse than the product loop on certificates, which refutes the hypothesis that the harness loop loses to the product loop on these tasks and does not support the hypothesis that it wins. Wall time is also level: the harness loop was faster in 11 of the 18 pairs, its median cell took 164 s against 179 s, and the two arms' totals differ by under one percent. The harness loop's spend is on record because its queries go through the harness: 352,494 output tokens and 553,676 cache-read tokens over 200 queries, but 3,005,288 cache-write tokens, because every query opens a fresh product session whose prefix is written to the cache again instead of read from it; the product loop keeps one session per cell and pays that once. The product arm's spend is not on this record: the slice that forwards the cell's model to the child and records the child's reported usage and cost merged after the run had started (the manifest's head carries it, the runs do not), so the next paired experiment carries both arms' spend.

The seventh record is the first cell the harness's own loop certified on the Claude Code route, immediately after the route began offering the harness tools natively: five model queries, five tool calls (explore, read the tests, read the stub, write the module, run the suite), no retry, one validation, 41 s from stamp to certificate, 2580 output tokens. The same environment took the product loop 59 and 63 s in the fourth record. Before that route change the same cell failed every query at the product's turn bound, which the route's note records.

The sixth record completes the product loop's pass over the bench: the nine tier-4 environments that are not held out, eighteen cells, every one certified in one attempt, 58 to 235 s per cell, 1151 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Tier 4 hands the implementer an existing module with planted defects and an immutable suite, which is why its cells are faster than tier 3's. Across the three fleets the product loop certified 48 of 48 cells at one attempt each, so on certificates this bench does not separate implementers at any tier for this product model; the bench's next slice is a harder tier and the six held-out environments, and every comparison below that reads attempts, wall time, and spend.

The fifth record is the same fleet plan on the nine tier-3 environments that are not held out: eighteen cells, every one certified in one attempt, 71 to 389 s per cell, 1844 s of wall time at two cells at a time. Tier 3 is therefore also a ceiling for the product loop on this bench, and a comparison that only counts certificates cannot separate implementers below tier 4; the separating measures at these tiers are attempts, wall time, and spend, of which the delegation record holds the first two and will hold the child's reported spend once the queued slice lands.

The fourth record is the Proving Ground bench's first fleet (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/`, thirty admitted program tasks): the product's own loop as the implementer of every cell, over the six tier-2 environments that are not held out, two repetitions each, seed 1, policy `bench-2026-09-07`, district `bench-h1`, two cells at a time, 984 s of wall time for the twelve cells. Every cell was certified in one attempt, so tier 2 is a ceiling for this implementer and the paired comparisons between the harness loop and the product loop run on tiers 3 and 4. The cells name the model `sonnet`; the product ran the installation's default model, which was measured as sonnet immediately before the run, because the delegation did not yet forward the cell's model to the child (the slice that forwards it and records the child's reported model is queued). The bench composition and tasks are those of commit `128e037bb`; the manifest records the head of the working tree at recording time.

The third record is the same district left running overnight: 22 slots on its thirty-minute cadence from 22:16 to 09:16 UTC, including the first slot the second record holds. The host restarted once; the slot due at 00:16 was not caught up, exactly as the shift driver's cadence rule states, and the relaunched process resumed the same ledger and cadence from 00:46 on the working tree of that moment, so the slots before the restart ran the tree at `88f6a1f2e` and the slots after it the tree at `38dd04165`, which the manifest records as the head. Every one of the 66 cells was certified in one attempt; the record holds all 22 shift ledgers, the 66 cell sessions, and the exports folded over them.

The second run is the live district's first slot after two defects the district itself exposed were fixed: a test check this Node rejected, and a runner that overlaid the whole fixture before validation and so discarded every edit to a fixture-supplied source file. Three program tasks, each with an immutable test suite, were implemented by the product in one attempt each and certified by the runner on the trees it left; the held-out task never entered the plan.

The first run is the first time an agent other than the harness itself was measured by the Proving Ground: two smoke environments at `isolation: none`, one child run per attempt recorded as `environment/delegation`, every delegation ending `completed`, facts exported for both sessions, both trajectories exported through the curator with one rewarded, and the observatory publishing both rows under the `claude-code` implementer with `runner` as the certificate executor of the certified one.

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Driver: boot the bench composition and run one fleet plan from a plan file,
4	 * then publish the observatory page and document, the session facts, the
5	 * trajectories, and `status.json` beside the report.
6	 *
7	 *   fleet-driver.ts <config> <plan.json>
8	 *
9	 * The plan file holds `{ name, environments?, tier?, domain?, heldOut?,
10	 * models: [{ provider, model, preset? }], ladder?, implementer?, repetitions,
11	 * seed?, policyVersion?, district? }`. Environment selection follows the
12	 * experiment driver's rules. A fleet plan runs every model entry over every
13	 * selected environment, which is how one run compares several product models,
14	 * one implementer against the same cells another run measured, or two agent
15	 * compositions over one route.
16	 *
17	 * An entry's `preset` is an agent preset id the composition's roster supplies;
18	 * it needs a config that composes one — the `with-presets` overlay — and a
19	 * preset no roster supplies refuses the plan before any cell runs.
20	 *
21	 * `ladder` is one rung per attempt — `[{}, { "model": { "provider": "…",
22	 * "model": "…" } }]` runs the first attempt on the cell's own route and the
23	 * second on the named one — and its length is each cell's attempt bound. A rung
24	 * that names no model runs the cell's own route, which is how a repeated-attempt
25	 * arm is written.
26	 */

29	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
30	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'

32	import { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'

35	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-observatory'

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Driver: boot the bench composition and run one frozen paired experiment from
4	 * a plan file, then publish the observatory page and document, the session
5	 * facts, the trajectories, and `status.json` beside the result.
6	 *
7	 *   experiment-driver.ts <config> <plan.json>
8	 *
9	 * The plan file holds `{ name, environments?, tier?, domain?, heldOut?,
10	 * repetitions, baseline, candidate, seed?, policyVersion? }`. `environments`
11	 * lists registered ids; when absent, every environment whose registered
12	 * `heldOut` flag equals the plan's `heldOut` (default false) is selected, then
13	 * narrowed by `tier` and `domain` read from each definition's detail. An arm is
14	 * `{ provider, model, ladder?, implementer?, preset? }`; `implementer` is
15	 * forwarded when the experiments service accepts it.
16	 *
17	 * `preset` is an agent preset id the composition's roster supplies, and it is
18	 * what makes two arms over one model route a comparison of two agent
19	 * compositions. It needs a config that composes a roster — the `with-presets`
20	 * overlay — and a preset no roster supplies refuses the plan before either arm
21	 * runs a cell.
22	 *
23	 * `ladder` is one rung per attempt and its length is that arm's attempt bound.
24	 * Its first rung is the arm's own route — `{}` or the arm's own `provider` and
25	 * `model` — and any other route is refused, so a cheap-then-strong arm is
26	 * written as the cheap model with `[{}, { "model": <strong> }]` and a downshift
27	 * arm as the strong model with `[{}, { "model": <cheap> }]`.
28	 */
29	
30	import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
31	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
32	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
33	import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer, EnvironmentRunRung } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
34	import { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
35	import type { EnvironmentId as EnvironmentIdType } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
36	import type { ExperimentPlan } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments'
37	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-observatory'
38	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'
39	import { jsonlFileSink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
40	
41	interface Arm {
42	  readonly provider: string
43	  readonly model: string
44	  readonly ladder?: readonly EnvironmentRunRung[]
45	  readonly implementer?: EnvironmentRunImplementer
46	  readonly preset?: string
47	}
48	
49	interface PlanFile {
50	  readonly name: string
51	  readonly environments?: readonly string[]
52	  readonly tier?: number
53	  readonly domain?: string
54	  readonly heldOut?: boolean
55	  readonly repetitions: number
56	  readonly baseline: Arm
57	  readonly candidate: Arm
58	  readonly seed?: number
59	  readonly policyVersion?: string
60	}
61	
62	const [configPath, planPath] = process.argv.slice(2)
63	if (configPath === undefined || planPath === undefined) throw new Error('experiment-driver requires <config> <plan.json>')
64	const plan = JSON.parse(await readFile(planPath, 'utf8')) as PlanFile
65	
66	const ctx = await boot('proving-ground-bench', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
67	try {
68	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the plan freezes against the settled registry.
69	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
70	  const experiments = ctx.get('experiments')
71	  const environments = ctx.get('environments')
72	  const observatory = ctx.get('observatory')
73	  const scorekeeper = ctx.get('scorekeeper')
74	  const trajectories = ctx.get('trajectories')
75	  if (experiments === undefined || environments === undefined || observatory === undefined
76	    || scorekeeper === undefined || trajectories === undefined) {
77	    throw new Error('the bench requires the experiments, environments, observatory, scorekeeper, and trajectories services')
78	  }
79	  const selected: readonly EnvironmentIdType[] = plan.environments === undefined
80	    ? environments
81	      .list({ heldOut: plan.heldOut ?? false })
82	      .filter((definition) => {
83	        const detail = definition.detail as { tier?: number; domain?: string }
84	        return (plan.tier === undefined || detail.tier === plan.tier) && (plan.domain === undefined || detail.domain === plan.domain)
85	      })
86	      .map(definition => definition.id)
87	    : plan.environments.map(id => EnvironmentId(id))
88	  const startedAt = new Date().toISOString()
89	  // An arm's optional ladder, implementer, and agent preset ride through as the experiments service defines its arm.
90	  const request: ExperimentPlan = {
91	    environments: selected,
92	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
93	    baseline: plan.baseline,
94	    candidate: plan.candidate,
95	    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
96	    ...(plan.seed === undefined ? {} : { seed: plan.seed }),
97	    ...(plan.policyVersion === undefined ? {} : { policyVersion: plan.policyVersion }),
98	    sink: jsonlFileSink('./experiment.jsonl'),
99	  }
100	  const result = await experiments.run(request)
101	  const snapshot = await observatory.snapshot()
102	  const page = observatory.render(snapshot, Date.now())
103	  await writeFile('observatory.html', page.html)
104	  await writeFile('observatory.json', `${JSON.stringify(page.json, null, 2)}\n`)
105	  const facts = await scorekeeper.exportFacts({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./facts.jsonl') })
106	  const exported = await trajectories.export({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./trajectories.jsonl') })
107	  const status = { type: 'result', plan: plan.name, environments: selected, startedAt, endedAt: new Date().toISOString(), result, rows: page.json.rows, facts, exported }
108	  await writeFile('status.json', `${JSON.stringify(status, null, 2)}\n`)
109	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(status)}\n`)
110	} finally {
111	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
112	}

1	# The Proving Ground bench: thirty zero-dependency program tasks in three
2	# domains, registered from their task.json files, run on the operator's Claude
3	# Code subscription through the harness's own agent loop (the LLM route) or
4	# through the product's own loop (the external implementer), and compared in
5	# frozen paired experiments. No cadence: the drivers beside this file run one
6	# plan each.
7	#
8	# The route serves three product models under one provider. Every arm of an
9	# experiment names one of them, so a comparison between models and a comparison
10	# between implementers both read from the same catalog. The product envelope
11	# around each query is the one model-visible input the log does not hold.
12	- id: llm-claude-code
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
14	  config:
15	    provider: claude-code
16	    models:
17	      - id: opus
18	        name: Claude Code opus
19	        productModel: opus
20	        contextWindow: 200000
21	      - id: sonnet
22	        name: Claude Code sonnet
23	        productModel: sonnet
24	        contextWindow: 200000
25	      - id: haiku
26	        name: Claude Code haiku
27	        productModel: haiku
28	        contextWindow: 200000
29	    effort: medium
30	    queryTimeoutMs: 300000
31	
32	# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor, for the CLI the route
33	# spawns per query, and for the product the external implementer spawns.
34	- id: subprocess
35	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'
36	
37	- id: sandbox
38	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local'
39	
40	# workspace-write over the cell session's own cwd, which the runner sets to the
41	# cell workspace. The configured root is the fallback for the agentless calls
42	# the runner itself makes: the checks run outside every session, so they still
43	# read the reservation the cells are denied.
44	- id: sandbox-policy
45	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy'
46	  config:
47	    mode: workspace-write

50	- id: bash
51	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox'

53	# A cell reads its own workspace and nothing above it: the runner registers the

55	# run log — as a denied root for the length of each run, and the barrier grants
56	# the cell's own workspace beneath it. The claim stays `none` because the E2
57	# candidate arm delegates to the product, which runs outside every fence this
58	# process installs.
59	- id: read-barrier
60	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
61	
62	- id: fs-read-barrier
63	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier'

65	# The filesystem tools resolve paths against the cell session's cwd, which the
66	# runner sets to the cell workspace; the policy loads first so writes and edits
67	# require an observed file.
68	- id: fs-local
69	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'
70	
71	- id: fs-observation-policy
72	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy'
73	
74	- id: tool-fs
75	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
76	
77	- id: goal
78	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
79	  config:
80	    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11
81	
82	- id: verification
83	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
84	  config:
85	    maxChecks: 32
86	    maxTextChars: 4096
87	
88	- id: environments
89	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
90	
91	- id: register-environments
92	  name: './register-environments.ts'
93	
94	# The default route of a cell agent; an experiment arm or a fleet plan names the
95	# model explicitly, so this only decides what an unnamed request runs.
96	- id: agent-default-model
97	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
98	  config:
99	    provider: claude-code
100	    model: sonnet
101	
102	- id: subagents
103	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
104	
105	# The product's own loop as an implementer, for the arm that measures it
106	# against the harness loop: unattended edits and the test command allowed,
107	# nothing else. Its spend is outside every limit this harness enforces.
108	- id: subagent-claude-code
109	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code'
110	  config:
111	    permissionMode: acceptEdits
112	    allowedTools:
113	      - 'Bash(node:*)'
114	
115	# `isolation: none` is the only claim the external arm can serve; both arms run
116	# under the same claim so the certificates compare.
117	- id: environment-runner
118	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
119	  config:
120	    isolation: none
121	    maxAttempts: 3
122	    evidenceMaxChars: 2048
123	
124	- id: fleet
125	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
126	  config:
127	    maxConcurrent: 2
128	    workspaceRetention: keep
129

131	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments'

137	    tokenBudget: 200000000

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Test driver: boot the curator composition, run one ordinary and one held-out
4	 * environment through the runner, then ask the curator for a `training` export
5	 * and an `evaluation` export of the same store. The e2e reads both manifests and
6	 * the evaluation lines the second one wrote.
7	 */
8	
9	import { mkdtemp } from 'node:fs/promises'
10	import { join } from 'node:path'
11	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
12	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
13	import { jsonlFileSink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
14	import { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
15	
16	const configPath = process.argv[2]
17	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('curator driver requires a config path')
18	
19	const ctx = await boot('curator-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
20	try {
21	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the runner creates agents only over the settled application.
22	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
23	  const runner = ctx.get('environmentRuns')
24	  const curator = ctx.get('curator')
25	  if (runner === undefined || curator === undefined) throw new Error('curator driver requires the runner and the curator service')
26	  for (const id of ['smoke:round-trip', 'smoke:reserved']) {
27	    const workspace = await mkdtemp(join(process.cwd(), 'workspace-'))
28	    await runner.run({ environment: EnvironmentId(id), workspace })
29	  }
30	  const training = await curator.export({
31	    purpose: 'training',
32	    sink: jsonlFileSink('./training.jsonl'),
33	    manifestPath: './training-manifest.json',
34	  })
35	  const evaluation = await curator.export({
36	    purpose: 'evaluation',
37	    sink: jsonlFileSink('./evaluation.jsonl'),
38	    manifestPath: './evaluation-manifest.json',
39	  })
40	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', training, evaluation })}\n`)
41	} finally {
42	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
43	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The contract a session's transcript is held under, pinned to the session log at creation. Every session this plugin sees start carries one `dataUse/terms` naming its client, agreement, purposes, residency, retention, and redaction profile before its first turn, so an export, a curator, or a client auditor reads the terms from the log rather than from the deployment that produced it. A later pin may narrow the terms and may never widen their purposes. Nothing here reaches a model request. Decision record: [the attributable-decisions Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md).
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: data-use
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use'
12	  config:
13	    clientId: acme-industrial
14	    agreementId: msa-2026-11
15	    purposes:
16	      - delivery
17	      - evaluation
18	    residency: eu-west
19	    retentionDays: 90
20	    redactionProfile: client-v3
21	```
22	
23	| Field | Meaning |
24	|---|---|
25	| `clientId` (required) | The client every session of this deployment belongs to. Cards hash it rather than showing it. |
26	| `agreementId` (required) | The agreement the terms come from. |
27	| `purposes` (required) | Non-empty subset of `delivery`, `training`, `evaluation`, each named once, in the order the agreement lists them. |
28	| `residency` (required) | Region the transcripts may live in. |
29	| `retentionDays` (required) | Positive whole number of days a transcript is kept. |
30	| `redactionProfile` (required) | Versioned redaction profile an export applies. |
31	
32	Every field is required and validated when the plugin loads: a deployment that cannot state its terms cannot pin them, and terms that admit nothing (`purposes: []`) or name no client would be a record no consumer could act on. A rejection carries `DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG`.
33	
34	## What a session start pins
35	
36	The service listens on `agent/session-start` and appends `dataUse/terms` with the configured defaults to any session that carries none. A resumed session already carries the terms it was created under, so it keeps them — the record states creation-time terms, not the deployment's current configuration.
37	
38	A composition without this plugin produces sessions with no terms at all; `termsOf(events)` answers `undefined` for them, and a consumer that requires terms decides for itself what to do with an unpinned session.
39	
40	## Service contract
41	
42	`pin(agent, terms)` validates the terms, refuses a widening, appends `dataUse/terms`, and returns the record as it was appended. `defaultTerms` is the deployment's configured terms, as every fresh session is pinned with. `termsOf(events)` is the exported fold consumers read; `widenedPurposes(standing, candidate)` names every purpose one candidate adds, and is what both the refusal and the invariant companion decide on.
43	
44	A pin whose `purposes` admit anything the session's standing terms do not is refused with `DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED` and appends nothing, because widening after the fact would turn a delivery-only transcript into training material. Every other field may be re-pinned freely — a shortened retention, a stricter profile, a corrected residency. An unusable field carries `DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS`.
45	
46	## The record
47	
48	| Event | Written when | Payload |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| `dataUse/terms` | At `agent/session-start` on an unpinned session, and at every accepted `pin()` | `clientId`, `agreementId`, `purposes`, `residency`, `retentionDays`, `redactionProfile` |
51	
52	The [persistence catalog](../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) carries the payload's declaration. The newest record is the session's terms.
53	
54	### Invariant companion
55	
56	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use/invariant` checks what the log can show: every record names a client, an agreement, a residency, and a redaction profile, keeps a positive whole-day retention, and lists a non-empty set of known purposes each named once; and no record widens the purposes the same session already carries.
57	
58	It cannot check anything outside the log: that the client and agreement exist, that the residency is where the transcript actually lives, or that any export applied the redaction profile named.
59	
60	## Model Experience
61	
62	None, as the terms are a durable record for exports, curators, and auditors; `dataUse/terms` is not a surface event, no prompt section or tool schema mentions it, and no model request is made or changed when one is appended.
63	
64	#### KV Cache effect
65	
66	Independent: the request surface is neither extended nor rewritten, so an already-reusable prefix stays reusable.
67	
68	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
69	
70	- **One export path enforces the terms** — [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-curator`](../curator/README.md) withholds every session whose terms do not admit its export's purpose, and a session carrying no terms at all is withheld for every purpose. `ctx.trajectories.export()` remains callable directly and reads no terms, so the pin binds the curated path rather than the data.
71	- **`purposes` is the only monotone field** — residency, retention, and the redaction profile may be re-pinned in any direction, because only widening purposes turns a transcript recorded under one agreement into material for another.
72	- **One set of terms per deployment** — the configured defaults are deployment-wide, so a process serving two clients pins both their sessions with the first client's terms unless every session is re-pinned by hand; per-agreement composition is the deployment's job.
73	- **No authority over who may pin** — as with `budget/caps`, any writer of a session's log can record terms; the companion bounds what a later record may say, it does not decide who may write one.
74

1	/**
2	 * Data-use terms: the contract a session's transcript is held under, pinned to
3	 * the session log at creation so every later reader — an export, a curator, a
4	 * client auditor — learns from the log alone what the transcript may serve.
5	 * A pin may narrow the terms and never widen their purposes, so a session
6	 * created for delivery cannot become training data after the fact. Nothing here
7	 * reaches a model request. The
8	 * [attributable-decisions Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use
11	 */
12	
13	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
15	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
16	// Type-only: resolves the `agent/session-start` event this service pins on.
17	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
18	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
19	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
20	import type { DataUsePurpose, DataUseTerms } from './types.ts'
21	
22	export type * from './types.ts'
23	
24	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
25	  interface Context {
26	    dataUse: DataUseService
27	  }
28	}
29	
30	/** Every {@link DataUsePurpose}, for validation and for option advertisement. */
31	export const DATA_USE_PURPOSES: readonly DataUsePurpose[] = ['delivery', 'training', 'evaluation']
32	
33	/** Stable error codes of terms this service refuses. */
34	export type DataUseErrorCode = 'DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG' | 'DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS' | 'DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED'
35	
36	/** Error returned when configured or pinned terms cannot hold a session. */
37	export class DataUseError extends HarnessError {
38	  /**
39	   * @param message - human-readable reason, naming the field at fault.
40	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
41	   */
42	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
43	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
44	  constructor(message: string, code: DataUseErrorCode) {
45	    super(message, code)
46	  }
47	}
48	
49	/** The deployment's default terms, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
50	export interface Config {
51	  /** The client every session of this deployment belongs to. */
52	  clientId: string
53	  /** The agreement the terms come from. */
54	  agreementId: string
55	  /** Non-empty subset of {@link DATA_USE_PURPOSES}, each named once. */
56	  purposes: DataUsePurpose[]
57	  /** Region the transcripts may live in. */
58	  residency: string
59	  /** Positive number of days a transcript is kept. */
60	  retentionDays: number
61	  /** Versioned redaction profile an export applies. */
62	  redactionProfile: string
63	}
64	
65	/**
66	 * The terms currently pinned to a log, or `undefined` when it carries none.
67	 * The pure fold — a consumer holding persisted events needs no service, and a
68	 * resumed session needs no catch-up because replaying the log IS the state.
69	 * @param events - session events in log order; other event types are skipped.
70	 * @returns the newest pinned terms, or `undefined` without any.
71	 */
72	export function termsOf(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): DataUseTerms | undefined {
73	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
74	    const event = events[index] as SessionEvent
75	    if (event.type === 'dataUse/terms') return event.data
76	  }
77	  return undefined
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * Whether `candidate` admits a purpose `standing` does not, which is the one
82	 * change a pin may never make.
83	 * @param standing - the terms the log already carries.
84	 * @param candidate - the terms a pin proposes.
85	 * @returns the purposes the candidate adds, empty when it only narrows.
86	 */
87	export function widenedPurposes(
88	  standing: DataUseTerms,
89	  candidate: DataUseTerms,
90	): readonly DataUsePurpose[] {
91	  return candidate.purposes.filter(purpose => !standing.purposes.includes(purpose))
92	}
93	
94	/** Data use (`ctx.dataUse`): the contract terms every session log states about itself. */
95	export class DataUseService extends Service {
96	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
97	    clientId: z.string().required(),
98	    agreementId: z.string().required(),
99	    purposes: z.array(z.union(['delivery', 'training', 'evaluation'] as const)).required(),
100	    residency: z.string().required(),
101	    retentionDays: z.natural().min(1).required(),
102	    redactionProfile: z.string().required(),
103	  })
104	
105	  private readonly defaults: DataUseTerms
106	
107	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
108	    super(ctx, 'dataUse')
109	    this.defaults = validateTerms(
110	      {
111	        clientId: config.clientId,
112	        agreementId: config.agreementId,
113	        purposes: config.purposes,
114	        residency: config.residency,
115	        retentionDays: config.retentionDays,
116	        redactionProfile: config.redactionProfile,
117	      },
118	      'DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG',
119	    )
120	    ctx.on('agent/session-start', ({ agent }) => {
121	      // A resumed session keeps the terms it was created under; only a session
122	      // that carries none is pinned, so the record states creation-time terms.
123	      if (termsOf(agent.session.events) === undefined) {
124	        agent.session.append('dataUse/terms', this.defaults)
125	      }
126	    })
127	  }
128	
129	  /** The deployment's configured default terms, as every fresh session is pinned with. */
130	  get defaultTerms(): DataUseTerms {
131	    return this.defaults
132	  }
133	
134	  /**
135	   * Pin narrower terms to one session and return the record as it was appended.
136	   * @param agent - the agent whose session the terms hold.
137	   * @param terms - the terms to record; their purposes may not exceed the session's.
138	   * @returns the terms exactly as they were appended.
139	   * @throws {@link DataUseError} when a field is unusable, or when the pin would
140	   *   admit a purpose the session's standing terms do not.
141	   */
142	  pin(agent: Agent, terms: DataUseTerms): DataUseTerms {
143	    const validated = validateTerms(terms, 'DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS')
144	    const standing = termsOf(agent.session.events)
145	    if (standing !== undefined) {
146	      const widened = widenedPurposes(standing, validated)
147	      if (widened.length > 0) {
148	        throw new DataUseError(
149	          `this session is pinned to purposes ${standing.purposes.join(', ')}, which the pin widens with ${widened.join(', ')}`,
150	          'DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED',
151	        )
152	      }
153	    }
154	    agent.session.append('dataUse/terms', validated)
155	    return validated
156	  }
157	}
158	
159	/**
160	 * Reject every field a durable record may not carry, then freeze the record.
161	 * @param terms - the candidate terms, from configuration or from a pin.
162	 * @param code - the classification a rejection carries.
163	 * @returns the terms as a detached record.
164	 */
165	function validateTerms(terms: DataUseTerms, code: DataUseErrorCode): DataUseTerms {
166	  for (const [field, value] of [
167	    ['clientId', terms.clientId],
168	    ['agreementId', terms.agreementId],
169	    ['residency', terms.residency],
170	    ['redactionProfile', terms.redactionProfile],
171	  ] as const) {
172	    if (value.length === 0) throw new DataUseError(`${field} is empty, so the terms state no ${field}`, code)
173	  }
174	  if (terms.purposes.length === 0) throw new DataUseError('purposes is empty, so the terms admit nothing at all', code)
175	  const seen = new Set<DataUsePurpose>()
176	  for (const purpose of terms.purposes) {
177	    if (!DATA_USE_PURPOSES.includes(purpose)) {
178	      throw new DataUseError(`purpose ${JSON.stringify(purpose)} is not one of ${DATA_USE_PURPOSES.join(', ')}`, code)
179	    }
180	    if (seen.has(purpose)) throw new DataUseError(`purpose ${JSON.stringify(purpose)} is listed twice`, code)
181	    seen.add(purpose)
182	  }
183	  if (!Number.isInteger(terms.retentionDays) || terms.retentionDays < 1) {
184	    throw new DataUseError(`retentionDays ${String(terms.retentionDays)} is not a positive whole number of days`, code)
185	  }
186	  return {
187	    clientId: terms.clientId,
188	    agreementId: terms.agreementId,
189	    purposes: [...terms.purposes],
190	    residency: terms.residency,
191	    retentionDays: terms.retentionDays,
192	    redactionProfile: terms.redactionProfile,
193	  }
194	}
195	
196	export default DataUseService
