content.content:
`foldTrajectory(meta, events)` is the pure projection behind the service and is exported for tests and offline tools. It is deterministic for the same inputs.

`foldTrajectoryReward(events)` decides the reward from the log's goal and verification events. A session whose last recorded [`verification/run`](../../verification/verification/README.md#what-a-runs-verdict-says) carries `verdict: 'tampered'` scores `outcome: 0` on the `tamper` basis whatever else the log holds, because a run that found the files it measures the task with changed says the measurement is void — a failed check means the work is incomplete, so folding the two would let a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task earn partial credit. Otherwise the verifier decides whenever a standard exists, an uncertified completion is undecided, and a log without a goal is unmeasured.

`foldTrajectoryStop(events)` decides how the session's last unit of work ended: its last turn for a session its own model route implemented, its last `environment/delegation` for one an external implementer did. A `turn/end` reason kind is carried verbatim, including a kind a plugin merges into `TurnEndReasonMap`, so a turn a plugin continued past an output-token ceiling still folds as `max-tokens`; a delegated attempt states the subagent seam's `completed`, `aborted`, `error`, `max-tokens`, or `refusal`. `budget` replaces either when a [`budget/breach`](../../guard/budget-policy/README.md#what-a-breach-does) ended the work: a turn the breach blocked, an attempt the runner's wall deadline cut short (`budget-deadline`), or a breach of the session's own caps after the last ended unit, which is how a delegated cell whose budget ran out before its next attempt ends. Each later turn or attempt restates the reason, so an attempt its rung's share cut short followed by one that ended on its own folds as `completed`. A log that ends inside an open turn is `interrupted`, and one that ended no unit of work at all is `none`. A breach scope or a delegated stop reason no owning package writes fails the fold, and the export reports that session under `skipped`.

`stopReason` exists because `outcome` cannot carry it: a session the budget stopped under a measured goal still exports `outcome: 0`, beside every session that ran to its end and failed. A consumer scoring rollouts reads a `0` as a failure only when `stopReason` is `completed` and masks it otherwise, and the exporter itself withholds nothing on those grounds.

`outcome` stays certificate-based, and `parity` is the auxiliary signal beside it. A run of [weighted cases](../../verification/verification/README.md#parity-and-what-it-does-not-decide) records its weighted pass rate on the `verification/run` event, and the record carries the last run's as its own `parity` field. It never replaces `outcome`: a pass rate is gameable by a candidate that overfits the failures it was shown and abandons the rest, so a session that passed most of a standard's case weight and one that passed none both export `outcome: 0` until a certificate covers the revision. A training run may shape a reward with `parity`; nothing may optimize it alone.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

fix(proving-ground): the bench exports through the curator, with the rules it lacked and each session's stop reason

A read-only audit on 2026-09-22 found the RLVR corpus path open on three
counts; this change closes each of them.

The curator on the export path. fleet-driver.ts and experiment-driver.ts
called ctx.trajectories.export(), the exporter that reads no terms and
redacts nothing: none of the 1,044 committed trajectory lines carries a
curation block, while the records' README called the export curator-gated.
Both drivers now call ctx.curator.export() for the purpose the composition's
data-use terms admit (training where they do, evaluation on the
subscription route), refuse a composition admitting neither before the
first cell runs, and write export-manifest.json beside the lines, which
record-run.mjs copies into the record. reexport-trajectories.mjs keeps the
raw fold for the uncurated records and refuses a curated one in both
modes. A keyless e2e runs both real drivers over a new mock-route overlay.
The README pair now says which export wrote which record.

The shipped rules. Six credential rules run ahead of the generic ones: PEM
private-key bodies with both armor lines kept (raw, JSON-escaped, indented,
CRLF, legacy-header, PGP, and truncated bodies), JWTs, AWS access key ids
and named secrets, and GitHub and Slack tokens. OpenRouter keys were
already covered by shipped:api-key, and a test now pins that. The IPv4
rule no longer matches a quad inside a longer dotted version such as
1.2.3.4.5. The manifest, now dsh-export-manifest/2, adds ruleRecords
beside ruleHits and never carries matched text.

The stop reason. dsh-trajectory/3 adds stopReason, folded from turn/end,
budget/breach, and environment/delegation: of the 99 reward-0 trajectories
on record, 71 ended on a budget breach and 4 on a provider error.
build-dataset.mjs masks a train-bound zero whose stop reason is not
completed and counts it under maskedNegatives, per reason; heldout.jsonl
keeps such rows.

content.text:
I rebuilt the export path so the bench drivers go through the curator, added the missing redaction rules, and put `stopReason` on the trajectory record. It's committed in the worktree (not pushed), and every check I ran is green except one unit test that was already failing before this change (below).

- **Worktree:** `/home/user/deepseek-harness/.claude/worktrees/agent-a3ec0ae0d50f8f7c6`
- **Branch:** `worktree-agent-a3ec0ae0d50f8f7c6`. It started on `master` (`47f943859`), which has none of the files the task names. It had no commits of its own, so I fast-forwarded it to `claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt` (`0235dc01e`) before starting.
- **Commit:** `adf28caf5`, one commit, 62 files. It ends with exactly the trailer you gave (`Claude Fable 5.1` + `Claude-Session`). That differs from this session's own default attribution line (`Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)`); I used yours as instructed.

**Audit numbers.** They reproduce exactly: 1,044 trajectory lines across 42 records, none with a `curation` block. Of the 99 reward-0 trajectories, the new fold gives 71 `budget`, 4 `error` and 24 `completed`. It also finds 17 certified trajectories that stopped on the budget, which is why the dataset builder masks only zeros and leaves positives alone.

**What changed**
- **A, curator on the path:**
  - Both bench drivers now call `ctx.curator.export()` and write `export-manifest.json` beside `trajectories.jsonl`.
  - The purpose comes from the composition's data-use terms, via `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/export-purpose.ts`: `training` where the terms admit it (the `with-openrouter` overlay), `evaluation` otherwise (the subscription route). A composition admitting neither is refused before the first cell runs.
  - `record-run.mjs` copies the manifest into the record.
  - `reexport-trajectories.mjs` keeps the raw fold for the existing uncurated records, but refuses a curated record in both modes, because re-folding would strip the redaction.
  - A new keyless `mock-route` overlay lets both real drivers run in e2e.
  - The `data/proving-ground/README.md` pair now says which export wrote which record, and that none were curated as of 2026-09-22. It also corrects a line claiming the curated export filters on `implementer` (it's the dataset builder that does).
- **B, redaction rules:**
  - Six new shipped rules that run before the generic ones: private key (PEM body only, BEGIN/END lines kept; also handles JSON-escaped, indented, CRLF, PGP and truncated bodies), JWT, AWS access key, AWS secret key (only when written under its name), GitHub token and Slack token.
  - OpenRouter `sk-or-v1-` keys were already covered by the `sk-` rule; a test now pins that.
  - The export manifest gains `ruleRecords` (how many records each rule fired in) beside the existing per-rule `ruleHits`, and holds no matched text. Its format is now `dsh-export-manifest/2`.
  - A first version of the private-key rule took 57 s on 20,000 BEGIN lines with no END; the final pattern takes 17 ms, and a test pins it.
- **IPv4:** the rule already required octets ≤255 and already left `v1.2.3.4` alone. The real false positive was a quad inside a longer version (`1.2.3.4.5` became `[redacted:ipv4].5`); that's fixed and tested. A bare `4.0.0.0` still reads as an address and is documented as a limitation.
- **C, stop reason:**
  - The record format is now `dsh-trajectory/3`, following the package's precedent that the format tag states which fields a record carries. `stopReason` is folded from `turn/end`, `budget/breach` and `environment/delegation`.
  - `build-dataset.mjs` masks a train-bound zero whose stop reason isn't `completed` and counts it under `maskedNegatives` and per reason in `maskedStopReasons`. `heldout.jsonl` keeps those rows, since a held-out run that exhausted its budget did fail.
  - I checked this end to end by temporarily re-exporting one record (since restored from git): its four budget-ended zeros were masked and its one real failure was kept.
- **E, Agent Note:** `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-22-curator-on-the-export-path.md`, with `.zh.md` and `.i18n.yaml`. I also added cross-links to it from items 1 and 3 of the RLVR note (both languages).

**Checks run, all passing unless noted**
- `pnpm run typecheck`, plus a later incremental host compile.
- Unit tests: trajectories and curator specs (75); the whole improvement and governance groups (498).
- Coverage scoped to both touched packages' `src`: 100% statements, branches, functions and lines.
- Keyless e2e, 9 files and 14 tests: curator, trajectories, the full bench suite including admission and the two new driver tests, environment-runner ×3, experiments, fleet, village-shift-zero. The two later purpose tests also pass.
- oxlint on every changed file (clean), knip (clean), duplication (0 clones), and the pre-commit hooks.
- `pnpm run doc-sync`: every gate passed except the config catalog, which was stale by one source line number. I regenerated it, re-ran that gate and pairing, and both pass; I didn't re-run the whole suite.
- **Already failing:** `scripts/proving-ground.spec.ts` `resolveRecordName` expects the name `...e7-attempts-5-t5-2`, but a record with that name has existed since `ed58a8f5d`. Unrelated to this change; I left it.

**Not done**
- The `village-live` and `village-claude-implementer` drivers still call the raw exporter. They have their own e2e suites, so I left them out of scope; the README names them.
- No committed record was re-exported. Every current record predates `stopReason`, so a dataset built today masks all 84 of its train-bound negatives as `(unstated)` until those records are re-exported.
- Both committed dataset manifests already failed `--check` before this change.
- Per your instruction I didn't edit the implemented notes. The dataset-fold note keeps its false "curator exported" claim, and the re-export note's statements about what the drivers call now describe the state before this change.
- No real (keyed) bench run was made, so the acceptance criterion that the next recorded run carries curated lines still needs one.
- A risk I noted but didn't fix: overlays pin one set of terms for every session, so a subscription arm run under `with-openrouter` would be pinned with training terms. No checked-in plan does this.
